Citigroup Inc. will release its third-quarter earnings report before the opening bell on Tuesday, Oct. 13.

Analysts expect the bank to report quarterly earnings of $2.62 per share, up from $2.26 per share a year ago. The consensus estimate for Citigroup's quarterly revenue is $23.72 billion. It reported $22.09 billion last year, according to Benzinga Pro.

Ahead of quarterly earnings, TD Cowen analyst R. Scott Siefers reinstated Citigroup with a Buy on Oct. 8 and set a $150 price target.

With the recent buzz around Citigroup, some investors may be eyeing potential gains from the company's dividends too. Currently, Citigroup has an annual dividend yield of 2.07%, with a quarterly dividend of 67 cents per share ($2.68 a year).  

So, how can investors exploit its dividend yield to pocket a regular $500 monthly?

To earn $500 per month, or $6,000 annually, from dividends alone, you would need to invest about $290,264, or around 2,239 shares. For a more modest $100 per month or $1,200 per year, you would need $58,079 or around 448 shares.

To calculate: Divide the desired annual income ($6,000 or $1,200) by the dividend ($2.68 in this case). So, $6,000 / $2.68 = 2,239 shares ($500 per month), and $1,200 / $2.68 = 448 shares ($100 per month).

Note that dividend yield can change on a rolling basis, as dividend payments and stock prices both fluctuate over time.

How that works: The dividend yield is computed by dividing the annual dividend payment by the stock's current price.

For example, if a stock pays an annual dividend of $2 and is currently priced at $50, the dividend yield would be 4% ($2/$50). However, if the stock price increases to $60, the dividend yield drops to 3.33% ($2/$60). Conversely, if the stock price falls to $40, the dividend yield rises to 5% ($2/$40).

Similarly, changes in dividend payments can affect the yield. If a company increases its dividend, the yield will also increase, provided the stock price stays the same. Conversely, if the dividend payment decreases, the yield will also fall.

With third-quarter earnings season kicking off, investors will be closely watching banking giants such as JPMorgan Chase JPM) and Citigroup C) this week for insights into lending activity, interest margins, and the broader economy.

However, smaller regional banking players Equity Bancshares EQBK) and Home BancShares HOMB) shouldn't be overlooked, as both are expected to deliver notable year-over-year earnings and revenue growth when they report Q3 results on Wednesday, October 14.

Equity Bancshares – EQBK

Headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, Equity Bancshares operates Equity Bank, providing commercial lending, consumer banking, agricultural financing, and wealth-related services across several Midwestern and Southern states.

For Q3, the Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for EPS of $1.31, an 8% YoY increase, with revenue projected to rise nearly 19% to $84.83 million.

Equity Bancshares has demonstrated impressive operating momentum, with Q2 EPS of $1.41 most recently jumping 42% from a year ago and beating expectations of $1.24 by nearly 14%. Its growth strategy, supported by acquisitions, expanding lending operations, and a broader deposit franchise, provides additional opportunities to increase profitability.

Notably, EQBK sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and further stands out with a 1.88% annual dividend yield and a reasonable 9X forward earnings multiple.

Home BancShares – HOMB

Based in Conway, Arkansas, Home BancShares operates Centennial Bank, offering commercial and consumer banking services, residential mortgages, and real estate financing, with a particularly strong presence in Arkansas and Florida.

Home BancShares is also positioned for another solid quarter, with the Zacks Consensus Estimate calling for Q3 EPS of $0.64, up nearly 5% YoY, and revenue expected to increase over 5% to $293 million.

The company's outlook is supported by healthy net interest income (NII), disciplined expense management, and contributions from its recently completed Mountain Commerce Bancorp acquisition. Encouragingly, Q3 NII is projected to increase more than 7% to $243 million.

HOMB currently sports a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), reflecting a favorable near-term outlook as it looks to build on its Q2 earnings beat, where quarterly EPS of $0.64 rose 10% YoY and topped expectations of $0.62.

Plus, HOMB trades at a reasonable 11X forward earnings multiple and currently offers a dividend yield over 3%.

Bottom Line

While the big banks will dominate headlines this week, Equity Bancshares and Home BancShares offer compelling exposure to regional banking growth.

What happens across this Global Week Ahead?

A backdrop of high energy costs and rising central bank rates, while

The latest U.S. and China macro data

Wall Street Q3 earnings, and

Turbulent bond markets point to a packed week ahead

Next are Reuters' five world market themes, re-ordered for equity traders—

(1) U.S. Q3 Earnings Season Kicks Off — with the Major Banks, of Course

It's the start of Q3 U.S. earnings season, and who better to kick things off than the banks?

Four of the six largest U.S. lenders, JPMorgan Chase JPM, Goldman Sachs GS, Citigroup C and Wells Fargo WFC, report on Tuesday, followed a day after by Morgan Stanley MS and Bank of America BAC.

Earnings are ‌expected to rise up to +20% relative to last year.

Still, the surge in Treasury yields to multi-decade highs has hurt shares — the KBW Bank Index is down around -13% from its peak in August.

Investors will be looking for signs that the recent spike in government borrowing costs may curb dealmaking and lending growth, as well as pressure funding costs across the industry.

(2) U.S. and French Government Bond Yields Keep Surging

Surging government borrowing costs are clearly luring some investors back to bonds as evidenced by the strong demand at the latest U.S. and Japanese auctions.

But do you really want to catch a falling knife?

That's the question for traders in the coming week as the bond selloff shows few signs of abating.

U.S. and French bond yields have hit fresh 24-year highs and market volatility is high.

The French-German 10-year bond yield spread, at around 136 basis points, was below 100 bps a month ago.

The speed and scale of the rise in the French risk premium is hurting Italian peers, the euro and European shares.

It's also led to some finger-pointing at the role of hedge funds — that fast-money group that has stepped up its presence in systemically important bond markets of late.

(3) On Wednesday, U.S. Consumer Price Inflation (CPI) Data for September Lands

A fresh look at U.S. inflation on Wednesday will be among the last key data released before the Federal Reserve decides whether to hike interest rates again to contain high prices.

The September CPI is set to show a 0.6% rise on a monthly basis. The core measure, excluding volatile energy and food components, is estimated to increase just 0.2%, according to a Reuters poll.

Thursday's Producer Price Index (PPI) numbers will further flesh out the inflation picture. Retail sales data is also out that day.

Core CPI for August rose at its fastest pace in four months, helping cement the Fed's first rate hike since 2023.

Bets on another hike when the Fed meets in late October have fallen back. A hot CPI report could change that.

Ecolab Inc. (ECL)

Citi moved Ecolab to its top pick across coverage, citing secular tailwinds in data center growth and visibility into strong order growth into 2027. The firm believes Ecolab's acquisition of CoolIT will continue to create a valuable platform for data center cooling and boost the organic growth profile of the company's consolidated business. Citi underwrites 10-12% growth in Life Sciences in the near term and 6-8% in Pest Control. The bank expects Ecolab to issue constructive medium-term targets on its High-Tech business at its Investor Day hosted at the Supercomputing Conference on November 17. While softer end-markets in quick-service restaurants and full-service restaurants present challenges, Citi expects these headwinds to be partially offset by growth levers in DishIQ and strong pricing execution. The firm believes Ecolab continues to execute well on its value pricing initiatives and should soon lap headwinds from pulp and paper markets.

Citi noted that as oil continues to trade at approximately $100 per barrel levels into the fourth quarter, and recent rate hikes pressure consumer sentiment, investors remain cautious on specialty chemicals. However, the bank believes companies demonstrating idiosyncratic outperformance through self-help actions, pricing ahead of costs, and continued volume growth could stand out despite overall demand levels.

For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 12, 2026 – Zacks.com releases the list of companies likely to issue earnings surprises. This week's list includes JPMorgan JPM, Citigroup C, Pepsi PEP, Micron MU and Nike NKE.

Estimates Keep Rising as Q3 Earnings Session Takes Center Stage

The Q3 earnings season takes center stage this week when JPMorgan, Citigroup and others report September-quarter results before the market's open on Tuesday, October 13th. This week's reporting docket, comprising 29 S&P 500 members, also includes companies outside the Finance sector, with bellwethers like Johnson & Johnson, Taiwan Semiconductor Company, and UnitedHealth also reporting quarterly results.

The expectation is that S&P 500 earnings will increase by +24.3% from the same period last year, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector remains a major growth contributor, but momentum is broad-based, with 15 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track for positive earnings growth in Q3. Importantly, the revisions trend remains positive and broad-based, highlighting a steadily improving outlook.

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates.

This positive revision behavior is not new; it extends a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and what we saw in Q3, constructive estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 7 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Aerospace, Construction, Industrials, Finance, and Transportation alongside Tech and Energy.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates remain under pressure for these 8 sectors – Conglomerates, Autos, Basic Materials, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Medical, Business Services, and Retail.

It is important to note that estimates for full-year 2027 have also been similarly trending higher, which we show a little later in this note.

Sector Focus: Broad-Based Strength

Q3 earnings are expected to be above the year-earlier level for 15 of the 16 Zacks sectors, with 6 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit growth. The multi-industry Conglomerates sector is the only one expected to have lower earnings in Q3 relative to the same period last year (earnings decline of –35.1%).
